summary.text: Eugene Vindman is the Democratic incumbent seeking a second term representing Virginia's 7th District. A retired Army colonel and former White House National Security Council attorney, he spent 25 years in the Army and later worked on war-crimes investigations in Ukraine before his 2024 election. According to his campaign website, his top priority is cutting taxes and lowering costs for working families.

paragraphs.text: Vindman came to the United States at age four with his family as refugees fleeing Soviet Ukraine and grew up in New York, attending public schools and a public university.

He earned a bachelor's degree from the State University of New York at Binghamton in 1997, a master's degree from Central Michigan University in 2005 and a law degree from the University of Georgia School of Law in 2009.
Commissioned through Army ROTC as a second lieutenant, he served from 1997 to 2022 as an infantry officer and paratrooper, with assignments in the 82nd Airborne Division and as a company commander.
Vindman later moved to the Army Judge Advocate General's (JAG) Corps, where he was an international law advisor in Iraq and senior prosecutor in the Army's busiest jurisdiction.
According to his congressional biography, he retired as a Colonel in 2022 after 25 years of service.
He served as a deputy legal advisor and agency ethics official on the White House National Security Council.

After retiring, he spent 18 months investigating war crimes in Ukraine, making 14 trips as a senior consultant for a State Department-funded program; Ballotpedia lists him as Director of Military Analysis and Prosecution Support for the Atrocity Crimes Advisory group.

Vindman ran for Congress in 2024 for the seat Abigail Spanberger left to run for governor, defeating Republican Derrick Anderson in the general election by 2.7 percentage points, and took office in 2025.
He serves on the House Armed Services Committee and the House Agriculture Committee.
According to his official biography, he and his wife Cindy raised their son and daughter in Dale City, Virginia.
